properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js ships SHA-1/SHA-2 implementations in the installed image; reachable by any future require() or transitive package even though no lesson file calls it directly.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js@4.2.0 is pulled in by merkletreejs, a direct dependency used by lesson 17_MerkleTree; merkletreejs falls back to crypto-js hashing internally when no hash function is supplied. MD5 has no call site in the tutorial code — the algorithms ship with the library either way. A second MD5 provider, md5.js@1.3.5, also ships in the same tree via create-hash ← ethereum-cryptography ← web3-utils ← merkletreejs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1 is collision-broken; its presence via the shipped crypto-js library is a posture fact even with no application call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Demo secp256k1 private keys pasted into every lesson script so the examples can sign transactions; these are the well-known Hardhat/Foundry dev accounts with no real funds, but they are live key material committed in first-party code (CWE-321/259 class), and every downstream signing chain in this repo runs on them.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The secp256k1 implementations the shipped node_modules image carries (elliptic, ethereumjs-curve, etc.); the application's own ECDSA signing runs through ethers' built-in curve code, which these packages complement in the dependency tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 is reached only through secp256k1@4.0.3 (native bindings) ← ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3 ← web3-utils ← merkletreejs. No application call site reaches elliptic: the tutorial's ECDSA signing runs through ethers v6, which uses @noble/secp256k1 instead. Availability is the inventory question here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Quantum-vulnerable key-agreement API surface present in the shipped dependency tree; this application never negotiates keys, but the capability ships.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js is pulled in by ethers (used by ethers' JSON keystore encryption); ships with the image though no lesson encrypts a keystore.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES available in the shipped crypto-js library; no lesson file performs symmetric encryption.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ethers itself hashes with @noble/hashes internally (keccak256, sha256); this entry is what makes that possible.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes@1.1.2 is a direct dependency of ethers@6.7.1 and is the hash engine behind ethers' keccak256: every ethers.keccak256 / solidityPackedKeccak256 call in lessons 17 and 18 executes this library's SHA-3 (Keccak) module. It also provides SHA-2 and BLAKE2b/BLAKE2s to the shipped tree (it does not provide BLAKE3 — see the rejected ALG-979eccf8).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@3.0.1 ships the scrypt memory-hard KDF. It sits in the ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3 ← web3-utils ← merkletreejs chain and has no direct call site in the tutorial. Note the application does perform scrypt at runtime — lesson 14_HDwallet's wallet.encrypt() keystore — but ethers v6 implements that internally, not via scrypt-js.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Pure-JS SHA-1/SHA-2 family shipped in node_modules; presence asset.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 provides secp256k1 ECDSA/ECDH (and EdDSA) to the shipped tree. It is a dependency of secp256k1@4.0.3 ← ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3 ← web3-utils ← merkletreejs (direct dep, lesson 17). No tutorial call site reaches it — the application signs through ethers v6/@noble/secp256k1 — but the library ships with the build and is loadable by any code that resolves it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 ships SHA-1, SHA-2 (224/256/384/512) and RIPEMD-160. It is a dependency of both elliptic@6.5.4 and ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3 in the web3-utils ← merkletreejs chain. No direct call site in the tutorial code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2@3.1.2 is the browser-compatible PBKDF2 polyfill in the ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3 ← web3-utils ← merkletreejs chain (together with its @types package). The application's own PBKDF2 use is separate and real: ethers v6 derives BIP39 mnemonic seeds with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, 2048 iterations (lessons 14/15/16) — reported as its own finding.
